course_description:
Provides a working understanding of some of the principal techniques used in business decision making. Topics include linear programming, transportation and assignment models, project scheduling and control, inventory models, decision theory and games. These techniques can be used to solve problems in areas as diverse as product mixing and blending, firm efficiency and benchmarking, project management, and multi-period financial planning. Problems and exercises are solved using Microsoft Excel or a simple menu-drive software package.

The quantitative techniques discussed in this course are collectively known asﾠ operations research ﾠ(OR) orﾠ management science ﾠ(MS) techniques. The OR/MS approach to business and economic decision making is scientific, relies on formal mathematical models, and involves the extensive use of computers. Students will learn how to use different types of software to implement the techniques taught in this course.

course_aims:
The aims of the course are to

The course does not aim to develop skills in the development, testing and application of MS&OR models for highly complex decision situations. However, the course does aim to give students an appreciation of where decision situations are of sufficient complexity to require the services of specialists in mathematical programming, systems simulation or other techniques. It is foundational for other courses on the topics covered in this course. It is also very valuable for the general understanding byﾠpractitioners in businesses and governments, i.e.,ﾠfor future leaders.ﾠ

learning_outcomes.description: Use mathematical methods of Operations Research and Management Science to model (i.e., mathematically formulate) various economic and business problems.
Solve the mathematical models of Operations Research and Management Science analytically, to find optimal solutions and perform sensitivity analysis.
Formulate the mathematical models of Operations Research and Management Science analytically, to find optimal solutions and perform sensitivity analysis, using computer software.
Communicate the results of model solving and explain their intuition using various digital means of communication and presentation.

assessment_details.task_description: These Weekly Quizzes are to be done by each student individually, in person only, during and at the Tutorials to which the student is officially signed up. These quizzes will be held during and at the tutorials (in person mode) of Weeks 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 (unless explicitly announced otherwise by the course coordinator via the blackboard). Only best 7 out of nine will count towards the final grade. Each quiz will be made available via Blackboard. (You must work in isolation while completing the quiz. Any direct or indirect collusion with others during this time may lead to charges of academic misconduct and a mark of zero for this assessment task.) Each quiz involves multiple choice questions that generally need to be answered based on the material from prior lectures and tutorials. It will require analytic (mathematical) formulations of a business problem and computations and involving a use of the software or/and an interpretation of its output. It may also request submission of workings (e.g., as screenshots from the spreadsheet or a photo of derivations on the paper, etc.) The typical timing is about 20 minutes, typically at the beginning of the designated tutorial. learning_activities.topic: Introduction to OR & MS; Optimization and Math Programming Operations Research (OR) & Management Science(MS) approach; constructing & solving OR&MS problems; OR&MS techniques; Break-even Analysis; Intro to Math Programming; Linear Programming;
Linear and Integer Programing A the graphical solution method for linear program (LP); characteristics of an LP problem; irregular problems; sensitivity analysis; examples
Linear and Integer Programming B Sensitivity analysis; LP in matrix form; the primal and dual LP; duality theorem; integer and 0-1 programs; mixed programs;
Transportation Problems; Intro to Projects Transportation and assignment problems. Key elements of project management; Gantt charts; CPM & PERT;

Project Scheduling and Control Project Scheduling and Control (Lecture): the project network; solution algorithms; Probability analysis of a project network; project crashing using CPM; estimating probabilities using PERT.
Decision Theory A terminology and notation of decision theory; the decision-making process and its components; criteria for decision making; decision-making with and without probabilities;
Decision Analysis B Bayesian analysis for accounting additional information; utility, different types of risk; basics of game theory
Inventory Models inventory terminology; notation; the basic EOQM; extensions to the basic EOQM.
Queueing Theory modelling of the arrival process; the waiting line; modelling of the service process; transient and steady states; M/M/1 systems; M/M/k systems; other systems;
Mid-semester Break No classes this week.
Production Analysis & Decisions A Production Theory: technical efficiency measures; Linear programming problems of production (Data Envelopment Analysis).

Production Analysis & Decisions B Production Theory: profit, revenue, cost; profit efficiency, revenue efficiency, cost efficiency and their estimations via linear and integer programming problems of production (Data Envelopment Analysis and Free Disposal Hull Analysis);
Review Review of Lecture 1-12 and tips about the Comprehensive Quiz
